packages.title: Federal Reserve, Clearing and Treasury
packages.question: Who may access, clear, settle or control public money and collateral across the Federal Reserve, Treasury and private clearing utilities?
packages.bluf: The September 20 legal-status and records-routing matrix establishes that the Federal Reserve has no single public/private status: the answer varies by actor, function, statute, record custody and remedy. The Board is a federal agency; the FOMC is an APA/FOIA agency; each Reserve Bank is a separate federally chartered corporation whose agency, instrumentality, employer, person and liability status changes by legal regime. Records likewise route by function and control rather than physical host: Bank-held material can be an FOMC record, a current-rule Board record, or a Bank record subject to the Banks' voluntary transparency policy and other lawful access routes. The companion appointment, removal and succession chain maps five distinct personnel constitutions from Governors and Reserve Bank directors through FOMC officers, SOMA management, the Inspector General and Bank general auditors; it also restores the August whole-government FRFS/National IT committee constitution to the direct package's discovery routes. The Wave 4 reconciliation confirms that the prior committee map was already substantial and classifies its bodies by legal effect: statutory Board/FOMC/Bank-board decisions, Board advisory and delegated routes, PSPAC policy advice, COP/Payments Committee/AFRC/ITOC enterprise governance, CPE/FRFS management, Richmond/National IT hosting and independent assurance. It distinguishes PCSC, PSPAC and the presidents' Payments Committee and preserves the unpublished charters, votes, materiality tests and application RACI as proof gaps. Wave 5 separates inspection and recommendation from approval, conditioning, direction, injunction, removal and institutional suspension. It finds extensive but nonuniversal audit, preserves GAO's monetary-policy exclusions and Dodd-Frank exceptions, defines the clean 2025 outside-audit limits, and locates actual stopping power in Board/Bank-board/FOMC/Treasury/court/congressional instruments rather than in the audit label itself. Wave 6 finds no unitary Federal Reserve crisis commander: insured-bank resolution, daylight and Discount Window credit, §13(3), FOMC/SOMA operations, payment and cyber incidents, Buddy Reserve Bank continuity, §248(h) intervention, cash logistics and Treasury fiscal-agent recovery have distinct legal principals, operators, books, finality and exit rules. It separates participant buddy banks from inter-Reserve-Bank continuity and service restoration from transaction reconciliation. Wave 7 reconstructs the twelve corporations' foundation: the Federal Reserve Act is the congressional charter; filing a district organization certificate created the body corporate; the Comptroller's separate certificate authorized business; and bylaws govern internally beneath federal law. It inventories all twelve current-posted bylaws and twenty-four Branches, distinguishes statutory member stock from ordinary equity, and identifies the direct St. Louis certificate plus exact missing constitutive, election, seal and title records. The September 20 congressional-oversight map shows why the Federal Reserve is not legally a fourth constitutional branch while preserving the real accountability critique: Congress created the System, controls its statutes and institutional design, confirms Governors through the Senate, mandates testimony, reports, audits and disclosures, and can amend or repeal the architecture; yet self-funding, long protected terms, nonconfirmed Reserve Bank presidents, GAO exclusions, OIG jurisdictional seams and monetary-policy exceptions deliberately insulate immediate policy operations. The vault-canonical factual spine and current Workbench extensions show how the Fed can retain the dollar unit and crisis backstop while private clearing moves into the middle and the twelve Reserve Banks specialize inside a common operating machine. The whole-site evidence supports contested functional unbundling and reduced daily visibility, not established castration, abolition, merger, private capture or removal. The September 20 dollar-issuance constitution shows that the Federal Reserve's role is a congressional statutory operating arrangement, not a private agreement or transfer of U.S. sovereignty. Congress defines the unit and legal-tender system; Treasury issues coins, retains capped United States-note authority and prints Federal Reserve notes; the Board orders and authorizes those notes; Reserve Banks issue notes into circulation and maintain central-bank balances; and private deposits and stablecoins remain legally distinct claims. Congress can restructure or replace that architecture by ordinary federal law, while executive orders, regulations and operator contracts cannot rewrite the statute. The companion congressional change history proves this is not merely theoretical: from 1927 corporate succession and the 1930s governance and gold rewrites through the 1977 objectives, 1980 monetary-and-payment reach, 2008 interest on reserves, 2010 emergency-credit limits and 2025–26 digital-money boundaries, Congress has repeatedly expanded, constrained and reallocated Fed powers. It also separates legislative dissolution from violation-based franchise forfeiture and the public dollar unit from Federal Reserve notes and private redeemable dollar claims. The Oklahoma City hearing audit shows that Congress was hardening the digital-public-money boundary, but the June 12 exchange did not establish illegal CBDC issuance or a §11(h) forfeiture case: no current Fed policymaker admitted ongoing work, the enacted §16A prohibition postdated the hearing, the House text predated it, and the public post-order projects reviewed do not establish creation of a U.S. central-bank liability. The September 20 payment-system mandate map shows that fostering safety and efficiency is a major Federal Reserve function but not a unitary third mandate parallel to Federal Reserve Act §2A. Congress supplied tool-specific powers that the Board, twelve Reserve Banks, private operators and co-regulators exercise through operation, access, intraday liquidity, rules, supervision, oversight and coordination; safety, efficiency and accessibility must therefore be tested at each lifecycle layer. The September 16 interest-rate constitution adds the missing rate-setting process: the FOMC target, administered tools, transaction benchmarks, auctions, traded yields and customer contracts are separate objects, and private, tax, insider, public-credit and credit-union below-market lanes have different authority and consequence. Its overnight-money companion follows the actual reserve-account, Fedwire, unsecured-credit, rollover and ON RRP mechanics beneath the policy rate and distinguishes Federal Reserve balances from commercial nostro/vostro claims. The September 18 DTCC whole-site refresh supports a regulated modular-conversion reading: DTCC is rebuilding legal submission, machine-readable reporting, operating hours, fund distribution, asset records and settlement interfaces while preserving incumbent membership, account, risk, correction and finality controls. AnnounceDirect, CMU CSV conversion, Fund/SERV tokenization access, 24x5 clearing, DTC tokenization and settlement modernization remain distinct objects with distinct proof gates rather than one common launch.

packages.title: Banks and Credit Unions — Federal and Four-State Legal Architecture
packages.question: What legally distinguishes banks from credit unions, which rules come from the federal government, and how do Florida, Wyoming, New York and Texas use their remaining charter, public-deposit, tax, supervision and digital-asset authority?
packages.bluf: The United States has overlapping bank and credit-union dual-charter systems rather than one national regime. Charter, ownership, regulator, insurer, account eligibility, public-funds permission, digital authority and operating state must be recorded separately. Florida and Texas maintain active state-bank and state-credit-union charters and admit credit unions to public deposits; New York maintains both charters but its ordinary local-deposit law still excludes credit unions; Wyoming charters banks and SPDIs but has no current state-credit-union law, so its credit unions are federally chartered even when state law admits them to public funds.

packages.title: Official Record Authority and Blockchain Crosswalk — 2026
packages.question: What does official record mean across federal records management, CFTC recordkeeping, securities ownership, corporate accounting, audit and public disclosure, and what changes when blockchain or DLT is permitted to hold the record?
packages.bluf: Official record is not one universal legal status. Authority, the exact recorded object, the accountable keeper and the consequence determine officialness for each purpose. The September 24 CFTC staff FAQ permits covered entities to keep qualifying regulatory records natively on-chain without a separate off-chain duplicate solely because blockchain is used, but the responsible entity must still satisfy content, retention, production, outage and inspection duties. That permission does not make blockchain consensus the controlling ownership record, a GAAP conclusion, sufficient audit evidence or settlement finality.

packages.title: From Atomic Settlement to Continuous Assurance — 2026
packages.question: Can atomic settlement, smart contracts, blockchain records and AI make real-time accounting and continuously updated financial statements practical, and how would the external audit change?
packages.bluf: Blockchain transactions can become continuously verifiable, smart contracts can make many controls continuously executable and AI can make large evidence populations continuously examinable, but none of those states is itself an audit. A continuously controlled event-to-books system is plausible; recognition, measurement, entity boundaries, valuations, exceptions, consolidation, disclosures and management judgment remain separate. Any continuous-assurance product would still require defined subject matter and criteria, an independent practitioner, sufficient appropriate evidence, a stated assurance level and a bounded report.

packages.title: QNT September 2026 Price Rise — Causal Audit
packages.question: What most plausibly caused QNT's September 24–26, 2026 price surge, how did the United Kingdom contribute, and what, if anything, was proved about direct QNT value capture?
packages.bluf: The sharp acceleration followed two official September 24 disclosures: The Clearing House selected Quant for the interoperability, orchestration and transaction-management layer of a planned U.S. tokenized-deposit network, while UK Finance reported the first live customer transactions on a Quant-built GBTD platform across seven banks. The U.S. selection is the strongest immediate catalyst; the UK operating receipt materially reinforced it. Neither announcement mentions QNT, token purchases, lockups, burns, staking balances or token-denominated institutional fees, so the move is evidence of market repricing around Quant software adoption, not proof of direct QNT value capture.
